subject.size_in_frame: from the waist up, about 0.60 of frame height, shrinking to her boots alone before she is gone

second_subject.note: the widening from sh014 recentres the black oval on the exact frame centre at about 0.30 of frame height, and it stays there for the rest of the sequence.

headroom: about 0.14 of frame height of root and hedge shade above her shoulders; once she is in, the whole upper third is hawthorn root and nothing else.
horizon_eyeline: Lens still at 0.25 m; spoil line across at 0.74. Her eyeline is gone from the frame within the first second — she is face-into-the-dark for almost the whole shot.

layers.fg: pale spoil crumbs along the bottom edge and, at the very end, her black ankle-strap boots kicking once, clean and unmarked
layers.mg: Alice going away from camera, arm then head then shoulders entering the oval
layers.bg: the flat black of the burrow, which swallows her without a change of shape

gaze.note: she is travelling away on the lens axis, so there is no lead room to give; the composition deliberately withholds a last look back at camera.

balance: Starts asymmetric (her mass left of the oval) and empties out to a centred, symmetrical frame — the picture resolves into the shape that sh016 then holds.
leading_lines: The hawthorn root arch and the spoil fan converge on the oval at centre; her own body becomes the last leading line, pointing into it.
eye_first: Her shoulders entering the dark, then the boots, then the black where both were.
constraint_binding: No cutaway and no reaction shot — the first impossible thing is played flat, so nothing in the composition marks the moment the hole proves too big: the framing, scale and lighting of the opening are identical before and after she fits through it. The black ankle-strap boots are kept clean, sharp and unambiguous in frame as they go, for the sh064 pay-off.
